policy_title: Ensure Democratic Consent for Onshore Wind and Protect Agricultural Land from Solar
stated: The Conservative Party will ensure democratic consent for onshore wind, ensuring local areas that host it directly benefit through measures like energy bill discounts. They will support solar in appropriate places, not on prime agricultural land, and prevent clustering of multiple solar farms.

source.quote: We will ensure democratic consent for onshore wind, striking the right balance between energy security and the views of their local communities. ...We will support solar in the right places, not on our best agricultural land.

bearing_set.reason: Restricting onshore wind via consent requirements and barring solar from prime agricultural land directly constrains the UK's renewable energy buildout, materially affecting the pace of emissions reduction and clean energy transition.

Explicitly proposes energy bill discounts for communities hosting onshore wind, a direct effect on household energy costs; broader supply constraints from the policy could also affect wholesale/retail energy prices for all consumers.

membership_note: O6 is the dominant bearing (renewable capacity constraints bear squarely on emissions trajectory and nature); O2 earns a real verdict because energy bills are explicitly named as both a sweetener mechanism and because restricting renewables has a concrete projected pathway to higher/more volatile household energy costs. O13 (clean-energy investment and industrial opportunity) was considered but left out as secondary to the direct O6 effect and insufficiently distinct to clear the non-negligible bar independently here.
